messages:
lena (Billing PM): :megaphone: Heads-up — we’re rolling out a change to burst handling and free-credit allocation on 2024-06-14 UTC. Please read and flag questions.

lena (Billing PM): TL;DR: 1) Per-route burst pools (accounts can enable route-level buffers that auto-borrow from a small global reserve). 2) The legacy one-time startup free-credit grant is replaced with a 90-day, account-age phased usage allowance that decays weekly. 3) Metering lag for minute-level quotas will be reduced from ~90s to ~30s.

lena (Billing PM): Why: routing-heavy apps hit global burst limits and seen spikes that caused noisy overage alerts for customers. This aims to reduce surprise throttles and make cost behavior smoother.

samir (Finance): Quick note — invoice lines will change names for burst usage. Old line: "burst_credit" -> New line: "route_burst_pool_usage". Expect small schema bump; no price change.

alex (Eng): Implementation notes for eng team: route pools are opt-in by route via the new API flag `burstPool: "route" | "global" | "disabled"`. Default for existing routes will be `global`. Example snippet:```json
{ "route": "/chat", "burstPool": "route", "poolSize": 200 }
```

tyler (DevEx): Will need an SDK patch + migration guide. I'll open a PR to add the `burstPool` param to client constructors and update examples. Target: small patch release on 2024-05-30.

maria (Support): For customer comms — we need a short FAQ about why some customers see reduced free-credit lumps and how the phased allowance works. I'll draft it and share this afternoon.

lena (Billing PM): Migration plan: existing customers keep full functionality; their routes default to `global` pool so behavior won't be stricter. New accounts get phased allowance by default. We will send opt-in invites for route pools for accounts that previously hit >2x minute peak.

alex (Eng): Ops question — how does auto-borrowing work? If route A empties, does it steal from route B preemptively?

lena (Billing PM): Answer: auto-borrowing pulls from the account's global reserve first; only if global reserve depleted will it attempt soft-borrow from other route pools in LRU order. Borrowing is logged and capped per-hour to avoid noisy cross-route bleeding.

samir (Finance): Accounting note — the phased allowance shows as a negative usage line labeled `phased_allowance_apr` for the first invoice month, then amortized. I'll sync with accounting to ensure clear mapping.

tyler (DevEx): FYI: SDKs must gracefully accept unknown burstPool values for one release to be forward compatible.

maria (Support): Draft FAQ Q: "Will my monthly spend increase with the new pools?" A: "No — pools are rebalancing, not new charges. They change how bursts are allocated; you will still pay for actual usage. If you want predictable throughput, consider Dedicated capacity."

billing-bot: Scheduled: Announcement email to users queued for 2024-06-01 16:00 UTC. Docs publish scheduled for 2024-05-28 09:00 UTC.

lena (Billing PM): Action items: @tyler open SDK PR, @alex add API flag + server-side logging, @maria draft customer FAQ and outbound, @samir coordinate invoice naming. I'll own the rollout notes and post the public changelog on the 28th.

alex (Eng): Got it. Will add telemetry to track cross-route borrow events.

samir (Finance): Will confirm how we show the phased allowance on trial accounts.

maria (Support): Will make a short canned response + escalation path for customers who see unexpected throttles.

lena (Billing PM): Thanks all — ping me in this thread if you hit blockers. :thumbsup:
